images.caption: Figure 1:Each iteration (1) samples a group of team executions per question (§3.1), (2) credits agent–skill pairs by contrasting these executions and diagnoses failures in a structured form (§3.2), and (3) aggregates the credit across questions into skill edits, each kept only if it does not lower the validation score (§3.3–3.4). The example is from one training run on LoCoMo single-hop questions, in which Agent 1 retrieves evidence and Agent 2 answers. In iteration 1, a failure that surfaces in Agent 2’s answer is traced to Agent 1’s retrieval, and a new retrieval skill is induced. In iteration 3, this skill is credited as harmful in the shown group but helpful across the iteration’s 16 groups, so it is refined rather than pruned. In Agent 1’s search queries,|denotes OR.
